# Remove Duplicates from Sorted Linked List

## Problem

Given the head of a linked list whose values are already in nondecreasing order, delete repeated nodes so that every remaining value occurs exactly once. You may visit each node no more than one time, and you are allowed to update the list's head pointer. Create a function that receives the linked-list head and returns the head of the list after duplicates have been removed.

### Example
```text
Input: 2->2->4->5->5
Output: 2->4->5
```

The duplicate occurrences of `2` and `5` are discarded, leaving one node for each distinct value.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Exploit the fact that equal values are adjacent in a sorted list, so duplicates can be removed during one forward traversal.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Keep one pointer for the last retained node and bypass any following nodes with the same value.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Handle an empty list, a single node, and a duplicate run at the tail while targeting O(n) time and O(1) extra space.

</details>
